----------------------------------------------------------------
EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN
----------------------------------------------------------------

1. IDENTIFICATION STRATEGY  

Method:  Fuzzy Regression-Discontinuity Design (RDD) in a panel setting (“difference-in-discontinuity”).  

Rationale:  
• The transfer of control rights is triggered mechanically when an observed accounting ratio falls below the contractually stipulated covenant level.  
• The forcing (running) variable – distance of the ratio from its threshold – is known ex-ante to the borrower and lender but is not continuously manipulable with‐precision at the quarterly reporting horizon (GAAP measurement, audit, lag).  
• Crossing the threshold sharply increases the probability of a binding renegotiation and of creditor influence, yet some violations are waived, so treatment is high-probability but not deterministic → fuzzy RDD.  
• Because we observe multiple quarters per firm, we can difference out firm-invariant heterogeneity and common shocks with firm and calendar-quarter fixed effects, yielding a difference-in-discontinuity.  

2. TREATMENT AND CONTROL  

Treatment variable  
TREAT_it = 1 if firm i in quarter t is in technical default on a given covenant  
              (ratio < contractual minimum after scaling), 0 otherwise.  

Control group  
Firm-quarters with ratio ≥ threshold but within a symmetric bandwidth h around the cutoff – i.e., firms “just compliant.”  

Running variable  
RUN_it = ( ActualRatio_it – CovenantLevel_i ) / |CovenantLevel_i|.  
Cutoff at RUN = 0.

Timing  
Quarter t when RUN turns weakly negative is the first quarter of (potential) treatment exposure. Multiple quarters can be treated; we estimate the contemporaneous effect and, in event-study extensions, dynamic leads/lags.  

3. KEY IDENTIFYING ASSUMPTIONS  

A1. Continuity of potential outcomes: In the absence of treatment, expected investment is smooth in RUN around 0.  
‒ Plausible: GAAP measurement, auditing, and multiple balance-sheet components make “fine-tuning” the ratio costly; no obvious discrete jump in fundamentals exactly at 0.  

A2. No precise manipulation (sorting) of RUN around 0.  
‒ Plausible but testable: use McCrary density test; inspect heaping at round numbers.  

A3. Local Stable Unit Treatment Value (no spillovers across bandwidth).  
‒ Reasonable: One firm’s covenant status does not directly change another’s investment within the same quarter.  

A4. First-stage relevance: Crossing 0 must meaningfully increase the probability/extent of creditor intervention.  
‒ Supported by institutional evidence and literature on post-violation renegotiations.  

A5. Independence of bandwidth choice: Estimates should be robust to reasonable bandwidth alternations and polynomial orders.  

4. THREATS TO IDENTIFICATION & MITIGATION  

T1. Anticipation or gradual adjustment (investment might start falling as the ratio approaches 0).  
 Mitigation: Include flexible polynomial in RUN; estimate local linear models; test for pre-trend using event-study coefficients at RUN > 0; restrict to very narrow bandwidths (e.g., |RUN| < 0.10).  

T2. Concurrent credit-demand shocks (e.g., macro downturn hits both ratios and investment).  
 Mitigation: Quarter×industry fixed effects; Macro-q and other opportunity controls in the RDD; difference-in-discontinuity already partials out time shocks, but we add controls.  

T3. Measurement error in accounting ratios moves observations across 0 spuriously (classical attenuation).  
 Mitigation: Use multiple covenant types separately; instrument actual TREAT with RUN<0 in first-stage (fuzzy RDD) so mis-measurement in RUN but not in treatment is accounted for; cluster SEs at firm level.  

5. R CODE OUTLINE  

```r
# --- 0. Packages -------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)
library(fixest)      # for high-dim FE regressions
library(rdrobust)    # for RD estimates
library(ggplot2)

# --- 1. Load data -----------------------------------------------
capex  <- fread("capex_compustat_crsp.csv")       # firm-quarter accounting
loans  <- fread("dealscan_loans.csv")             # loans & covenants

# --- 2. Merge & keep covenant sample ----------------------------
dt <- merge(capex, loans, by = c("gvkey","quarter"), all.x = TRUE)

# --- 3. Construct running variable ------------------------------
# example: current ratio covenant
dt[, run := (curr_ratio - curr_ratio_thresh)/abs(curr_ratio_thresh)]
dt[, treat := as.integer(run < 0)]                       # reduced-form
dt[, abs_run := abs(run)]

# --- 4. Bandwidth restriction (baseline h = 0.25) --------------
h  <- 0.25
sample <- dt[abs_run <= h & !is.na(run) & !is.na(capx_ppe)]

# --- 5. Main fuzzy RD with firm & time FE -----------------------
# first stage: probability of actual renegotiation (if measured) or treat
est1 <- feols(treat ~ qpol(run,1,0) | gvkey + quarter, data = sample,
              cluster = "gvkey")

# second stage: investment
est2 <- feols(capx_ppe ~ qpol(run,1,0) | gvkey + quarter |
              treat ~ qpol(run,1,0), data = sample,
              cluster = "gvkey")          # 2SLS inside fixest
summary(est2)

# --- 6. rdrobust (non-parametric, no FE) -------------------------
rd_out <- rdrobust(y = sample$capx_ppe, x = sample$run, fuzzy = sample$treat)
summary(rd_out)

# --- 7. Robustness: alternative bandwidth / placebo -------------
for (hh in c(0.15,0.30,0.40)){
  tmp <- sample[abs_run <= hh]
  est <- feols(capx_ppe ~ qpol(run,1,0) | gvkey + quarter |
               treat ~ qpol(run,1,0), data = tmp, cluster="gvkey")
  print(list(bw = hh, coef = coef(est)["fitted(treat)"]))
}

# Placebo threshold at RUN = +0.2
placebo <- dt[run > 0.2 & run < 0.45]          # artificial cutoff at 0.3
placebo[, run_p := run - 0.3]
feols(capx_ppe ~ qpol(run_p,1,0) + I(run_p<0) |
      gvkey + quarter, data = placebo, cluster="gvkey")

```

6. EXPECTED RESULTS  

Theory predicts that shifting control to creditors tightens the financing constraint and reduces discretionary investment, especially when agency conflicts are severe. I expect:  
• Quarter-on-quarter capex/PPE falls by 0.3–0.6 pp (≈ 10–20 % relative decline from a 3 % sample mean).  
• Effects are magnified for high information-asymmetry firms (small, young, low analyst coverage) and mitigated for firms with low agency costs (high insider ownership).  

7. VALIDITY CHECKLIST SELF-ASSESSMENT (RDD)  

C1: No sorting around cutoff ……… 0.8  
C2: Covariate balance/continuity … 0.8  
C3: Correct functional form ……… 0.7  
C4: Strong first stage ……………… 0.9  
C5: Appropriate inference ………… 0.9  

(1 = clearly satisfied; scores summed /5 = 4.1)
